svg.text: Fishball scanner: one harness for the handheld and the desk unit
JP5, the 2x10 expansion header: the pins the harness uses
ALIVE: high while the scanner runs
The board's own connectors, each at an opening in the case wall
the unit as a USB device
console and JTAG; its VBUS is the 5 V rail itself (note 2)
Each knob's common pin and switch return,
each key's other leg and the light's cathode
go to ground. The pull-ups are the Pico's own.
1.8 V logic, driven by the FPGA
Power: the button turns the switch on. The Pico turns it off (OFF high)
once the scanner has stopped. The charger works on or off.
DEBUG's VBUS is wired straight to the board's 5 V rail. On battery,
plug DEBUG in only through a cable without VBUS, or with the unit
switched off: the PC then powers the board and the panel.
JP5's pins are FPGA pins: the serial link and ALIVE need the bitstream
to bring PS UART0 and a GPIO out to them, and the audio needs the
radio core's I2S block (the roadmap's step 9).
